notes: Main alias route: every page under reference/5.1/<Module>/ (About topics excluded) was read for two independent statements of a command's aliases: the YAML front matter key 'aliases:' and the NOTES passage 'Windows PowerShell includes the following aliases for `<Cmdlet>`:'. 384 pages; 140 NOTES passages (all parsed); 172 names in NOTES passages and 181 in front matter; their union gives 183 aliases. Three more come from About/conceptual pages (man, md, ise). Each alias entry's 'evidence' says which of the two statements carries it.

Function route: reference/5.1/Microsoft.PowerShell.Core/About/about_Built-in_Functions.md is an explicit list of the functions 'loaded into every PowerShell session ... not included in any module ... defined in the PowerShell engine itself'. All 12 named functions plus A: through Z: are taken from it and cross-checked against the cmdlet and About pages listed per entry. It confirms the expected mkdir, more, ImportSystemModules, Get-Verb and the drive functions.

On some 5.1 pages the front matter and the NOTES passage disagree. Each case is an omission, never a conflicting definition: Get-History front matter omits 'h'; Remove-Item front matter omits 'rmdir'. The 11 CimCmdlets pages other than Get-CimAssociatedInstance (gcim, gcls, gcms, icim, ncim, ncms, ncso, rcie, rcim, rcms, scim) have front-matter aliases but no NOTES passage.

The documentation does not distinguish the aliases a module exports from those the engine defines. These documented 5.1 aliases belong to commands outside the Core/Management/Utility set: CimCmdlets (12: gcai, gcim, gcls, gcms, icim, ncim, ncms, ncso, rcie, rcim, rcms, scim); Microsoft.PowerShell.LocalAccounts (15: algm, dlu, elu, glg, glgm, glu, nlg, nlu, rlg, rlgm, rlu, rnlg, rnlu, slg, slu); PSWorkflow (1: nwsn). about_Modules.md:23-24 says PowerShell 'automatically loads an installed module the first time you use a command from the module'. I believe, without documentary support, that these aliases are defined by their modules and appear in Get-Alias only once the module is imported, while invoking one by name triggers autoloading. On the same belief, the aliases of Microsoft.PowerShell.Core/Management/Utility commands, plus man, md and ise, are engine built-ins present at start. Each alias carries 'commandModule' (from the page's 'Module Name:' front matter) so a consumer can make this cut. The 5.1 docs also say LocalAccounts is 'not available in 32-bit PowerShell on a 64-bit system' (reference/5.1/Microsoft.PowerShell.LocalAccounts/Add-LocalGroupMember.md:199).

Aliases whose target is a function, not a cmdlet: clear and cls -> Clear-Host (Clear-Host.md calls it a function, though its page sits under Module Name Microsoft.PowerShell.Core), man -> help, md -> mkdir. ise -> PowerShell_ISE targets the ISE executable; the documentation gives the command as `PowerShell_ISE`, not an exact definition string.

The 'pwsh75' field compares each 5.1 alias with the 7.5 cmdlet reference at the same commit. Its NOTES passages group aliases under 'All platforms:', 'Windows:' and 'Linux and macOS:'. 'windows only' means the alias would not exist in pwsh 7 on Linux. The 7.5 reference adds one alias absent from 5.1 docs (gerr -> Get-Error, a 7.x cmdlet) and has no other alias missing from the 5.1 set.

7.5 documentation contradicts itself on several aliases that 5.1 lists: Set-Content (sc), Export-PSSession (epsn), Import-PSSession (ipsn), Trace-Command (trcm) and New-PSSessionConfigurationFile (npssc) keep the alias in their 7.5 front matter, but their 7.5 NOTES passage names none. curl and wget (Invoke-WebRequest) and lp (Out-Printer) are in neither in 7.5; 7.5 lists only iwr for Invoke-WebRequest. differences-from-windows-powershell.md never states that curl, wget, sc or lp were removed.

7.5 New-PSDrive.md NOTES passage reads 'PowerShell includes the following aliases for `Get-PSDrive`:' and then lists ndr and mount. It is a copy error: the 5.1 New-PSDrive page and unix-support.md:262 both give mount -> New-PSDrive.
man on Linux: unix-support.md:261 lists man (-> help) as not available on Linux or macOS, but 7.5 about_Built-in_Functions.md:49 heads its section '`help` (alias: `man`)' with no platform qualifier.

7.5 Clear-Host lists cls under both 'Windows:' and 'Linux and macOS:' and clear under 'Windows:' only, which agrees with unix-support.md:254. 7.5 Invoke-Item lists ii with no platform group, and is taken here as all platforms.

unix-support.md:273 says its table 'doesn't include aliases unavailable for cmdlets that don't exist on non-Windows platforms'. The 'windows only' and 'command not in the 7.5 reference' statuses cover those cases (for example gsv, sasv, gcim, gwmi). One alias contradicts it: 7.5 Receive-PSSession.md groups rcsn under 'All platforms', while unix-support.md:176 says Receive-PSSession isn't available on Linux or macOS. rcsn is marked 'windows only (command unavailable on Linux/macOS)'.
Belief, not documented: curl, wget, sc and lp no longer exist in PowerShell 7 on any platform, Windows included. The 7.5 NOTES passages omit them, but no page states their removal.

using-aliases.md heads its table 'Compatibility aliases in Windows' and says 'The aliases in this table are Windows-specific'. The page speaks of current PowerShell across platforms, not of 5.1 against 7. Its row 'md | mkdir | New-Item | ni' does not say md is an alias of New-Item. about_Built-in_Functions.md:81 makes md the alias of the mkdir function.

Two 5.1 pages, Clear-Variable.md and Export-Alias.md, say 'PowerShell includes the following aliases' where all the others say 'Windows PowerShell includes'. The wording makes no difference to the content.

Select-String.md (5.1) NOTES remarks that the official alias prefix for Select-* is 'sc' and that 'sls' is an exception. That is about naming convention: 'sc' is the alias of Set-Content, not of any Select-* cmdlet.

differences-from-windows-powershell.md:418-421: 'AllScope was removed from most default aliases' in PowerShell 7. By implication the 5.1 default aliases carry the AllScope option. No page lists the option per alias.

Functions of 7.5 against 5.1 (about_Built-in_Functions at both versions): 7.5 drops Get-Verb (a Utility cmdlet from 6.0 per cmdlet-versions.md:128/421), ImportSystemModules and more (removed per differences-from-windows-powershell.md:964-967). It adds cd~ (7.4) and exec (7.3.1). It says mkdir and the drive-letter functions are not defined on non-Windows systems.

Excluded as module functions: PSConsoleHostReadLine is defined by the PSReadLine module, which the 5.1 console host loads automatically (reference/5.1/PSReadLine/PSConsoleHostReadLine.md:23-29). It is therefore present at start in the console host but not 'with no module'. Functions exported by any other module are likewise out of scope.
'pause' is documented in lower case (about_Built-in_Functions.md:36). Function lookup is case-insensitive, and the casing Get-Command would show is not documented.
